title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous and next pages: Grothendieck is treating projective structures on a complex curve through the Schwarzian derivative. For a local uniformizer t (an étale map U→A^1) and another uniformizer s he defines G_t(s) = -2 s'''/s' + 3 (s''/s')^2. This is -2 times the classical Schwarzian {s,t}. G_t(s) is invariant under homographies of s and transforms like a quadratic differential (G(t,s)dt^2). He reads the equation G_t(s)=μ(t) as the equation for horizontal sections of a P^1-bundle with connection, i.e. a projective connection or sl_2-oper. The previous page sets up a dictionary between its solutions s, Riccati solutions λ = -s''/s', and solutions α = s' of a first-order equation. The previous page ends with a theorem: for a complete algebraic curve X over C there is a unique section μ (the quadratic differential μ(t)dt^2) such that the solutions of G_t(s)=μ are the 'uniformizing' functions. These are the branches of the inverse of the universal covering map X^an~ → disc (or plane or sphere), i.e. the Fuchsian (Koebe–Poincaré) projective structure.

This page finishes the theorem. The solutions form a sheaf, a torsor under PGL_2 (the dual M^∨ of a rank-2 local system: horizontal sections). It is described as a sheaf of functions on X^an containing all the 'uniformizing' functions.

Corollary: when X is complete (and presumably hyperbolic), μ(t) is an analytic section of O_U, determined canonically by the uniformization.

Question 1: is μ algebraic, i.e. is the uniformizing projective connection an algebraic quadratic differential (a rational function of t)? He names the 'first interesting cases' X = P^1 minus three points and X = an elliptic curve minus a point.

Question 2 concerns an algebraic family of curves X→S over an algebraic base. Fibrewise, μ gives analytic functions on X that are algebraic on each fibre. Are they algebraic on X? Does the construction have an algebraic meaning independent of the topology of C, i.e. is it compatible with automorphisms of the field C? The last line is unclear; it possibly asks whether S is a solution of some equation.

In modern terms these are:
- the algebraicity of the Fuchsian projective connection, which is the accessory-parameter problem;
- its behaviour in moduli, i.e. whether the Fuchsian section of the affine bundle of projective structures over M_g (or M_{g,n}) is holomorphic or algebraic, and whether it is Aut(C)-equivariant.
errors: P^1 minus three points is not really an 'interesting' case for algebraicity. The Fuchsian projective connection there is forced by symmetry: its accessory parameters are determined. It is the classical rational Schwarzian of the inverse of the modular λ-function, given by a hypergeometric equation, so μ is algebraic (rational). The genuinely open cases are P^1 minus four or more points and the once-punctured torus (Lamé accessory parameter). The note does not record that the three-point case is trivially yes.

Implicitly, the theorem needs X hyperbolic (or the appropriate notion of uniformization in the parabolic or elliptic cases), and μ must be allowed to have the prescribed second-order poles at punctures. The note does not spell this out.

Not an error, but the expected answer to question 2 is negative, and the note gives no hint of that. Zograf–Takhtajan show the Fuchsian section is only real-analytic, not holomorphic, on Teichmüller/moduli space: its ∂̄ is the Weil–Petersson form. So it is neither algebraic in families nor Aut(C)-invariant.

ideas.what: Equation -2s'''/s'+3(s''/s')^2 = μ, whose solution sheaf is the local inverse of the uniformization, as horizontal sections of a projective connection
ideas.modern_name: Fuchsian (uniformizing) projective structure / sl_2-oper; Schwarzian equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schwarz, Klein, Poincaré; modern sheaf/connection formulation Gunning (1966), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers)

ideas.what: Question whether the uniformizing quadratic differential μ is algebraic, with test cases P^1−3 points and elliptic curve minus a point
ideas.modern_name: Accessory parameter problem; algebraicity/transcendence of Fuchsian uniformization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Poincaré, Klein; Keen–Rauch–Vasquez (1979, punctured tori/Lamé); Chudnovsky; Takhtajan–Zograf

ideas.what: Question whether in an algebraic family X→S the fibrewise uniformizing projective connections form an algebraic object, independent of the topology of C (Galois-invariant)
ideas.modern_name: Holomorphy/algebraicity of the Fuchsian section of the bundle of projective structures over moduli; Galois-equivariance of uniformization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Zograf–Takhtajan (1987): the Fuchsian section is real-analytic, ∂̄ = Weil–Petersson form; Bers

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether the canonical (uniformizing) projective connection has an algebraic meaning, invariant under Aut(C), in families. This is an early algebro-geometric framing of the question later answered negatively by Zograf–Takhtajan (non-holomorphic dependence on moduli). The framing is close to his later anabelian concern with Galois action versus complex topology, but the question itself is answered in the literature.
missed.quote: Sont-elles algébriques (?), et [ont-elles] une signification algébrique, indépendante de la top. des corps
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's interest (1970s) in arithmetic aspects of uniformization, predating Esquisse d'un programme and Belyi-type questions. Mathematically it is settled (negative in families; transcendence questions on accessory parameters remain partially open).

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, natural question about the algebraicity of the Fuchsian projective connection and its Galois invariance in families, posed by Grothendieck in an unpublished note. It is historically interesting as a precursor to anabelian themes, but the problem is classical (accessory parameters) and its family version was resolved negatively by Zograf–Takhtajan. The P^1-minus-three-points case is actually trivial.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely refers to the dual M^∨ (horizontal sections / local system) and 'sous-faisceau ... de fonctions uniformes(?) sur X^an'; the correction above 'uniformisantes' seems to read 'uniformes' or similar.
'Premier cas intéressant : X = P^1_C − trois pts, ou X = courbe elliptique moins un point' – the last line reads 'moins un point', not '[?] un point[?]'.
'Est-elle algébrique ?' – 'Est-elle' is written above a struck-out word; reading confirmed.

In 'Autre question', it reads roughly 'quand X (supposé ... compact? ...) varie avec un paramètre algébrique formant une variété algébrique S, i.e. ... X → S, on trouve comme μ des fonctions analytiques sur X, algébriques sur les fibres'.
